answer: Newcomers start on a mesa, a probationary tier where work is real but rewards cannot yet be transferred. Each accepted task adds a rung to a trellis of verified history, checked by a rotating panel against the brief within five days, and only after ten rungs from three different clients does promotion follow. As the tide of verified work rises, duplicates are exposed: copied output collapses the whole trellis and forfeits all trial credit. One honest user climbs once; a thousand fakes must each climb the same ladder, paying a thousand times the effort for nothing transferable until then.
